tip.explanation: This command removes stopped containers, unused networks, dangling images (images without associated containers), and build cache. Use this regularly to reclaim disk space and keep your Docker environment clean.  The `-a` flag ensures all unused resources are removed, including volumes.  Use with caution as data will be lost, consider using `docker system prune -v --dry-run` to see what would be removed before deleting anything.
This command shows all containers in your system, both running and stopped. Use -a flag to see stopped containers too. Essential for container management and debugging.

tip.description: Follow container logs in real time
tip.explanation: Useful for debugging and monitoring. The --follow flag keeps the connection open to see new logs as they appear.
